`Cached autocomplete` [docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:38-46]

    ## Cached autocomplete
    
    Each prefix node caches ten terminal-node references ordered by frequency.
    Since frequencies only increase, updating the changed terminal plus the cached
    winners suffices along its ancestor path. The public top-six query walks the
    prefix and slices its winners. Requests above cache capacity use full traversal.
    Mutation cost and memory increase in exchange for cheaper repeated prefix reads.
    [MICROBENCHMARKS.md](MICROBENCHMARKS.md) compares both paths on synthetic data and
    checks they return identical suggestions; timing is not asserted in tests.

`Suggestions, duplicates, and snapshots` [README.md:163-172]

    ### Suggestions, duplicates, and snapshots
    
    Autocomplete reads cached winners after walking the prefix. Spelling correction
    proposes changes only for zero-hit terms; it does not silently rewrite queries.
    Suggestions are based on indexed stems. SimHash candidates share a 16-bit band;
    Hamming distance verifies them with a configurable threshold of at most three.
    
    Binary snapshots include document metadata, snippet text, and both positional
    fields. Writes use a unique temporary file, fsync, and rename. A checksum rejects
    partial/corrupt data; startup can rebuild from MongoDB. Old `index.json` snapshots

    ## Snapshot and stream recovery
    
    Snapshots contain metadata, full snippet text, and both positional fields. The
    binary format starts with a magic/version marker and SHA-256 checksum; lengths,
    document ordinals, and position gaps use unsigned base-128 varints. Unique temp

`Binary snapshots and legacy support` [docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:76-85]

    ## Binary snapshots and legacy support
    
    Sorted external IDs get compact internal ordinals. Posting ordinal gaps and
    position gaps use varints; strings are length-prefixed UTF-8. The checksum detects
    partial writes and damaged payloads. Writers fsync unique temp files then rename;
    legacy delta-encoded JSON is still accepted and validated. Full snippet text is
